Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae and tables produced by the GCE Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Electronic calculators may be used. Start each question on a fresh page.
enonce_intro_markdown:
The yields, to the nearest kilograms of 150 fruit trees, are given in the table below

| Yield, $x$ kg | 10 - 14 | 15 - 19 | 20 - 24 | 25 - 29 | 30 - 34 | 35 - 39 | 40 - 44 | 45 - 49 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Number of trees, $f$ | 4 | 9 | 18 | 28 | 39 | 30 | 15 | 7 |

Estimate, to two decimal places,
incertitudes: Question 2 (b) : l'écart type est calculé avec le diviseur $n = 150$ (valeur 8.10) ; avec le diviseur $n - 1$ on obtiendrait 8.12. Le sujet dit « the standard deviation of the yields » : la distribution des 150 arbres est traitée comme une population.

Question 2 (c), (d), (e) : la médiane et les quartiles sont des estimations lues sur la courbe ; le corrigé donne la valeur obtenue par interpolation linéaire sur la courbe (31.55, 25.66, 36.92, écart quartile 5.63) ; une lecture graphique correcte donne environ 31.5, 25.7, 36.9 et 5.6. Le sujet n'imprime pas de figure : le corrigé décrit le tracé de la courbe et donne ses points.

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) the standard deviation of the yields.
questions.corrige_markdown:
$$\sigma^2 = \frac{\sum f x_m^2}{\sum f} - \bar{x}^2 = \frac{155230}{150} - \left(\frac{4670}{150}\right)^2 = 1034.8667 - 969.2844 = 65.5822$$

$$\sigma = \sqrt{65.5822} = 8.0983\ldots$$

**Standard deviation $\approx 8.10$ kg** (divisor $n = 150$, the distribution being treated as the whole population).

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Draw a cumulative frequency curve for the data.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Because the yields were rounded to the nearest kg, the **upper class boundaries** are $14.5, 19.5, 24.5, \ldots, 49.5$. Plot each cumulative frequency against the upper boundary and join the points with a smooth curve (an ogive), starting from $(9.5, 0)$.

| Upper boundary, $x$ | 9.5 | 14.5 | 19.5 | 24.5 | 29.5 | 34.5 | 39.5 | 44.5 | 49.5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cumulative frequency | 0 | 4 | 13 | 31 | 59 | 98 | 128 | 143 | 150 |

**Scales:** horizontal axis, yield $x$ (kg) from 9.5 to 49.5 (for example 2 cm for 5 kg); vertical axis, cumulative frequency from 0 to 150 (for example 2 cm for 20 trees). Label both axes. The curve is S-shaped and steepest between $x = 29.5$ and $x = 34.5$, where the class frequency is largest (39).

The values $n/4 = 37.5$, $n/2 = 75$ and $3n/4 = 112.5$ are then read off on the vertical axis (parts (d) and (e)).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Using the cumulative frequency curve, estimate

(d) the median yield
questions.corrige_markdown:
The median is the value with cumulative frequency $\dfrac{n}{2} = \dfrac{150}{2} = 75$. On the curve, draw a horizontal line from $75$ on the vertical axis to the curve, then down to the $x$-axis.

This point lies between $(29.5, 59)$ and $(34.5, 98)$, where the curve is nearly a straight line; linear interpolation gives

$$\text{Median} = 29.5 + \frac{75 - 59}{98 - 59} \times 5 = 29.5 + \frac{16}{39} \times 5 = 29.5 + 2.05 = 31.55$$

**Median yield $\approx 31.55$ kg** (a graph reading of about 31.5 kg is acceptable).

questions.enonce_markdown: (e) the quartile deviation of the distribution.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The quartile deviation (semi-interquartile range) is $\dfrac{Q_3 - Q_1}{2}$.

**Lower quartile**, cumulative frequency $\dfrac{n}{4} = 37.5$, between $(24.5, 31)$ and $(29.5, 59)$:

$$Q_1 = 24.5 + \frac{37.5 - 31}{59 - 31} \times 5 = 24.5 + \frac{6.5}{28} \times 5 = 24.5 + 1.16 = 25.66$$

**Upper quartile**, cumulative frequency $\dfrac{3n}{4} = 112.5$, between $(34.5, 98)$ and $(39.5, 128)$:

$$Q_3 = 34.5 + \frac{112.5 - 98}{128 - 98} \times 5 = 34.5 + \frac{14.5}{30} \times 5 = 34.5 + 2.42 = 36.92$$

$$\text{Quartile deviation} = \frac{36.92 - 25.66}{2} = \frac{11.26}{2} = 5.63$$

**Quartile deviation $\approx 5.63$ kg** (graph readings give about 5.6 kg).
